extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Diplomat (diplomats, analysts, policy professionals, business readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria for a company’s public response (apology, withdrawal, investigation, attribution) to a controversial advertising campaign—especially for ads released in foreign/local markets. Focuses on transparency, timeliness, responsibility, and cultural sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize and withdraw offending content
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi apologized and withdrew the commercial completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page reports that Audi "apologized and withdrew the commercial completely" (action taken on July 19). Use of immediate withdrawal and an explicit apology is presented as a primary remediation step for an offensive ad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of the apology (public vs. one-on-one)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi apologized for the ad, yet not publicly on its website, but through one-on-one emails to whoever complained to Audi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights that the apology was sent personally to complainants rather than posted publicly, implying that public acknowledgement on official channels is an important expectation and that private responses may be perceived as insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of responsibility (internal vs. joint venture/agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi has repeatedly emphasized that the responsible department is its joint venture in China, as the ad was created by this division and was “produced exclusively for the Chinese market.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company’s statement attributes responsibility to its China joint venture. The page presents such attribution as part of the response narrative—potentially read as distancing the parent brand—which evaluators may treat as a deflective (vs. fully accountable) posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to investigate internal controls and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: "The responsible department of the joint venture has arranged a thorough investigation of the internal control and coordination processes so that an incident like this can be excluded in the future."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page quotes Audi’s commitment to a "thorough investigation" of internal controls and coordination. Promising investigation and corrective process changes is presented as a concrete remediation/assurance measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness of the response
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercial "immediately received a wave of backlash. On July 19, Audi apologized and withdrew the commercial completely."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline (rapid backlash followed by apology and withdrawal) is emphasized; prompt action is framed as an important quality of an effective crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sexism and objectification in advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Chinese netizens condemned Audi for sexism and objectification of women; the ad compared buying a used car to finding a wife and showed a mother-in-law inspecting the bride’s body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article foregrounds public condemnation for sexism and objectification. A substantive criterion for acceptable ads is that they must not demean or objectify groups (here, women); awareness of cultural trends and sexist tropes is required to avoid such fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization does not excuse offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi noted the ad was "produced exclusively for the Chinese market."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page treats the "produced exclusively for the Chinese market" explanation as part of the response but implies that local production does not absolve the company from adhering to overall company values and global standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency/creative partner accountability and public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Advertising Age, the ad was made by Ogilvy & Mather Beijing... But up till now, Ogilvy China hasn’t commented on the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the ad’s agency and the lack of comment from Ogilvy China, suggesting that effective crisis handling includes agency accountability and timely public statements by third-party creators when controversies arise.
